subject: Crestline MSA & Order Form — telemetry / IP carveouts questions
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@crestline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@crestline.com>, legal@crestline.com
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — telemetry and IP carveouts

Kimberly — attaching our redlines (MSA + Order Form) for your review. High-level items we care about up front: 

1) Telemetry / logs: we need a clear statement of what Redwood stores from customer API calls. Do you retain full prompt/response text in logs? How long are those logs retained? We require that logs containing customer confidential data be deletable on request and that any telemetry used for product improvement be anonymized and not include customer proprietary content.

2) Output ownership / title: we are proposing explicit language that Crestline retains title to outputs generated from our proprietary prompts and content (customer-owned output). We are open to Redwood using generated outputs for aggregate analytics only if they are de-identified and not used to train models.

3) Feedback license: we cannot grant a broad training license to our data or outputs. If Redwood wants to use opt-in telemetry for model improvements, it must be limited, anonymized, and documented with an opt-in flow.

4) PHI / regulated data carveout: we need assurances this data will not be used for training and that audit logs exist for deletion/retention requests.

Can you confirm which of these are acceptable and provide proposed redline language for the telemetry and feedback sections so our counsel can review? We also flagged a handful of Order Form clauses around warranty and indemnity tied to output quality — please see the attached PDFs.

Thanks — can we aim to have a proposed internal response by Monday so we can move to legal redline exchange next week?

— Sara
Senior Counsel, Crestline Therapeutics

Attachments: Crestline_MSA_redlines_20280517.pdf, OrderForm_Crestline_draft_trackchanges.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@crestline.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@crestline.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — telemetry and IP carveouts questions

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the redlines. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Ben (Customer Success) so we can give you a coordinated reply. Quick clarifications from product that will inform our legal position: 

- Runtime logs: Redwood retains request/response payloads in our runtime logging for up to 30 days by default for debugging and abuse monitoring. We also have an option (Private Deployments / Dedicated) to disable retention at rest.
- Telemetry metrics (aggregated latency, token counts, route usage) are retained longer for analytics but do not include full prompt text.
- We already support a customer opt-out for model improvement (a checkbox on account settings) that prevents data from being added to research training corpora.

Laura / Ben — can you propose language that: (a) commits to deletion of stored logs on request (with an SLA for deletion), (b) defines "anonymized/aggregated" telemetry, and (c) explicitly carves out PHI and regulated data from any feedback license? Sara, if you have a target clause or sentence we can mirror, that helps.

I’ll pull together a short redline for the telemetry and feedback license sections and send by end of day Monday. If it looks like many open issues remain we should schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call next week.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@crestline.com>, Michael Chen <mchen@crestline.com>
Date: Sat, 19 May 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed language — telemetry, deletion SLA, and feedback license

Kim / Ben / Sara — I reviewed Crestline's redlines and sketched out proposed positions that balance product needs with the customer's requests. Key proposals (attached as "redwood-proposed-telemetry-clause_20280519.docx"):

1) Telemetry retention and deletion SLA: 
- Redwood will retain request/response payloads for debugging for a default retention period of 30 days. Upon written request from an authorized Crestline admin, Redwood will remove request/response payloads associated with Crestline's account from live systems and backups within 14 calendar days, except to the extent retention is required by law.

2) Definition of telemetry used for product improvement: 
- "Telemetry" will be defined as aggregated, non-personally identifiable metrics (token counts, latency distributions, model selection, error rates) and will not include customer prompt or output text. Any use of customer-provided prompts/outputs for model improvement will require an explicit, documented opt-in.

3) Feedback license carveouts and PHI: 
- Redwood requests a narrow license to use opt-in customer feedback (explicitly identified by the customer) for model improvement. This license will exclude PHI, regulated data, and any content expressly designated by the customer as Confidential.
- Proposed contract language: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use Customer Opt-In Feedback solely for the purpose of improving Redwood's models or services, provided that such Feedback excludes PHI and information the Customer designates as Confidential; Customer may revoke this license at any time by written notice, and Redwood shall cease using such Feedback within 30 days of revocation."

4) Auditability: 
- We can commit to providing an audit log showing deletion actions and timestamps upon request for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private plans. For hosted customers, we will provide deletion confirmation and scope.

These positions are intended as negotiation starters and to address Crestline's core concerns. If Crestline needs a contractual guarantee of "no training on any customer content under any circumstance," that is a tougher ask for hosted plans but possible for Private/Air-gapped deployments with a corresponding pricing / commitment model.

I attach the drafted redline text for the MSA/Order Form sections. Kimberly — if you want, I can prepare a side-by-side clause to send to Crestline counsel tomorrow.

— Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-telemetry-clause_20280519.docx
From: Michael Chen <mchen@crestline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@crestline.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — telemetry and IP carveouts questions

Laura / Kimberly — thanks for the quick review and the draft language. A few points from our side: 

- Crestline's preferred outcome is a contractual guarantee that our customer-generated prompts and outputs will not be used to train Redwood models for any hosted tiers. We understand Private/Dedicated can be handled differently, but we need that guarantee for hosted SaaS users.
- The deletion SLA of 14 days is workable, but we also need clarity on backups and whether deleted logs can reappear during restore windows. Can you make an explicit statement that Crestline-deleted payloads will be removed from backups within the same 14-day window wherever technically feasible?
- For the "opt-in" model improvement license: Crestline expects an explicit UI opt-in for each environment (test/prod) and an admin-level reversal path; please confirm.

For timing, we need proposed redline text by end of Tuesday so our outside counsel can do a formal redline exchange on Wednesday. Also please confirm whether you can provide an evidence package (SOC2 control mapping for log retention and deletion) as part of the procurement pack.

If any of these requests are not acceptable, please call them out explicitly so we can evaluate options (e.g., move to Dedicated for guaranteed non-training, or accept a documented deletion process plus SOC2 attestation).

— Michael
Director, IT Contracts, Crestline Therapeutics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <mchen@crestline.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@crestline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — telemetry and IP carveouts questions

Michael / Sara — summary and next steps: 

1) Hosted non-training guarantee: Redwood cannot offer a global contractual prohibition on training on customer content for our standard hosted SaaS without significant product and commercial changes. Options: 
   a) We can include a firm, auditable opt-out mechanism for model improvement that prevents your account data from being included in research/model training corpora (this is available today and we will spell it out contractually).
   b) For a contractual "no training" guarantee, we can move the account to Dedicated capacity or a Private deployment under a separate commercial arrangement (we can price this and share the timeline).

2) Deletion SLA and backups: Laura proposes 14 calendar days for live system + best-effort for backups; we will include explicit language stating Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to remove Crestline payloads from backups within 14 days and will disclose any material limitations. We will provide a deletion confirmation and a log entry.

3) Opt-in mechanics: We will provide an admin-level opt-in/opt-out UI per environment, and revocation will be honored within 30 days for use already shared for model training (Laura's draft reflects 30 days). We will include this flow in the procurement pack and document it in the Order Form.

4) Evidence / controls: We can include a SOC 2 mapping and a short controls summary for log retention and deletion; full SOC 2 report will be provided under NDA during procurement.

Next steps: Laura will send the side-by-side redline for the MSA telemetry and feedback clauses by EOD tomorrow. I will also schedule a 30-minute call for legal-to-legal on Wednesday (please expect an invite). If Crestline prefers to finalize via redline exchange only, confirm and we will expedite.

Proposed timeline: 
- Tue EOD: Redwood internal redlines delivered to Crestline counsel
- Wed: legal redline exchange or 30-min call as preferred
- Fri: finalize Order Form commercial items (if no major legal gaps)

Thanks — we want to keep this moving.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
